requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM location WHERE location_id = 'LOC_004' AND name = 'TechCorp Munich Analytics Lab' AND org_id = 'ORG_001' AND plot_no = '50' AND street = 'Königsplatz 3' AND city = 'Munich' AND state = 'Bavaria' AND country = 'Germany' AND active = 1
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (LOC_004 after LOC_003); the only location the task creates
org_id not stated; ORG_001 (TechCorp) from the location's name and the acting user's organisation, the only TechCorp organisation in the seed; not in the benchmark check
'50, Königsplatz 3' read as plot_no '50', street 'Königsplatz 3', as the benchmark check reads it
acting user USER_001 is an admin, so may create locations (policy section 2)

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on every requirement (same four: the location at LOC_004, the two nodes selected by serial number, the storage node's status change), every cell and value, and all three dispositions (kept); they differ only in the wording of assumptions, so there is no disagreement to log. Seed facts re-checked at merge: Aisha Williams is USER_004 and Carlos Rodriguez USER_003 (both ORG_001, active); ORG_001 is TechCorp; LOC_003 is the highest location; no seed serial number or location name is near the new ones, so no boundary stay is needed; the acting user USER_001 holds the admin role. The benchmark's Node B check is carried by two requirements with the same source: the registration cells and the status change to maintenance. Its cost 6400 reads the request's malformed '$64,00' as written; a run that writes 64000 fails both the benchmark check and requirement 3. The create requirements add name and org_id (inferred, not stated), which the benchmark checks do not test.
